notes: Summary: Nighthawk builds a modular contact center orchestration layer used by 150+ mid-market retailers. Want to add LLM-powered agent assist + direct tool-calls into their existing ticketing and refunds APIs.
Primary ask: reliable, idempotent tool-calling for create/update ticket flows, automated refund authorization with audit trail, rapid escalation path to human ops via API callouts.
Traffic profile: normal 10k msgs/day across customers; seasonal spikes 6-8x during flash sales (~120k msgs/day). Concern: tail latency and rate-limited 3rd-party ticketing endpoints.
Latency/throughput targets: 95th pct latency <250ms for agent assistance suggestions; end-to-end ticket creation workflow SLA <1.2s (goal) but will accept async fallback for heavy spikes.

Model preferences: want to test open models (LLaMA variants) and Redwood-verified LLMs; quantized variants acceptable for cost. Important: deterministic tool-call payloads and schema enforcement (function/tool calling).
Security/compliance: must keep PII out of hosted logs for EU customers; require KMS encryption for any persisted KV cache, SSO (SAML) for admin console, SOC2 required before production go-live.

POC scope agreed: 2-week POC: 1) agent-assist latency baseline on hosted-api; 2) tool-calling adapter to their refunds microservice (idempotent endpoint); 3) spike simulation with synthetic load to validate fallback policies.

POC success criteria: <250ms median suggestion latency, correct 99% idempotent ticket creations (no duplicates), graceful fallback to async queue for <5% requests under peak without user-visible failures.
Notes from 2026-03-02 call (ffl-2394823): 'If the model triggers duplicate refunds that's a showstopper' — head of ops. Need strict confirm-step UI + audit log for refunds.

Integration details: customer uses an internal ticket system (OpsAPI v3) behind VPC with mutual TLS. Wants Redwood to call a gateway function that enforces rate limits and translates payloads. SE: build small lambda adapter recommended.
Security review: sent security FAQ (drive link) on 2026-02-28; customer asked for sample data retention policy and option to disable K/V caching for EU accounts.

Technical risk: external ticketing endpoint returns 429s under spike; customer prefers Redwood to implement automatic backoff + queue-to-worker fallback and per-customer routing to alternative endpoints.

Pricing sensitivity: mid-market — willing to commit reserved capacity if cost predictability and SLOs are met. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations to reduce token costs for templated prompts.
Quotes/phrases: 'We need 0-tolerance for duplicate refunds' (Head of Ops). 'Prefer private control plane for audit logs' (VP Security).
Communication cadence: weekly POC syncs (AE+SE+Eng), ad-hoc security calls.

Action items assigned: SE (Priya) to deliver POC runbook + sample tool-calling adapter by 2026-03-15; AE (Ethan) to push legal DPA draft to customer legal; Customer infra to provide mTLS certs for test gateway.
Customer sentiment: pragmatic, cautious on refunds, excited about quick agent-assist wins that reduce AHT.
Reference links inserted: jira INFRA-7821 for adapter work; SEC-1294 for DPA exceptions.

Internal notes: consider recommending Dedicated pools for consistent latency during marketing spikes; include automatic fallback to 'create-ticket (async)' webhook that returns 'accepted' for the agent UI.
Follow-ups: schedule architecture review with Redwood runtime team to validate KV cache encryption and quantization behaviors (target wk of 2026-03-17).
